message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"12","text":"The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, roaming about discerningly and closely examining the conduct of each person in the church—who is about to sin—so that, when caught through admonition by the one who presides, that person perhaps may not carry the sin through at all. They should bring back those who desert their posts, so that those who assemble do not fail to listen to the discourses, and so that they may be able, by the word of truth, to clear away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For whenever they have lain fallow for a long time, they become material for fire. They should also find out who are sick in the flesh and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may present themselves; and they should provide what is necessary according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should attend to these and similar matters.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι ἔστωσαν ὀφθαλμοί","chosen":"should be the bishop’s eyes, roaming about discerningly","rationale":"Preserves both the image of the deacons as eyes and the prudent, discerning movement expressed by the participle and adverb."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν","chosen":"closely examining the conduct of each person in the church—who is about to sin","rationale":"Treats τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν as the question directing the deacons’ close investigation without removing the abruptness of the Greek."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν","chosen":"They should bring back those who desert their posts","rationale":"Retains the military image in λειποτάκτας and the restorative force of ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","chosen":"so that those who assemble do not fail to listen to the discourses","rationale":"Provisionally takes τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject of ἐπιλείπειν and ἐπακούειν as its infinitival complement. An infinitive construction with ἐπιλείπω is attested in the consulted lexical evidence, including Antiphon 5.17, but that evidence does not determine Clement’s attachment or exclude the alternatives recorded below."},{"source_quote":"τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας ἔκ τε βιωτικῶν συνπτώσεων καὶ ὁμιλιῶν κακῶν λόγῳ ἀληθείας καθαίρεσθαι","chosen":"by the word of truth, to clear away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations","rationale":"Preserves the image of discouragements falling upon the heart, their two stated sources, and λόγῳ ἀληθείας as the means of clearing them away."},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","chosen":"For whenever they have lain fallow for a long time, they become material for fire","rationale":"Retains the agricultural image of lying fallow and the subsequent fire image while leaving the plural subject unresolved."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν","chosen":"They should also find out who are sick in the flesh","rationale":"Renders μανθανέτωσαν as ascertaining who is ill while retaining the explicit bodily qualification κατὰ σάρκα."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","chosen":"and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may present themselves","rationale":"The consulted evidence for passive ἐπιφαίνω includes coming into view and presenting oneself, supporting “present themselves.” Any more specific sense of visiting the sick would be a contextual inference because Clement supplies no explicit object meaning “visit them.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","issue":"The syntax permits materially different analyses. The main text takes τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject of ἐπιλείπειν and ἐπακούειν as its complement: “so that those who assemble do not fail to listen.” Alternatively, ἐπακούειν may depend on συνερχομένους, yielding “those who assemble to listen,” while intransitive ἐπιλείπειν means that they do not fall away or become wanting. A further alternative makes the deacons the unexpressed subject of transitive ἐπιλείπειν: “so that they do not abandon those who assemble to listen to the discourses.” The consulted lexical evidence attests senses such as leaving behind, failing someone, becoming wanting, and construction with an infinitive, but it does not settle Clement’s syntax. The supplied Greek is not being treated as corrupt.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"συνπτώσεων","issue":"The supplied edition has the unassimilated spelling συνπτώσεων. The normalized spelling συμπτώσεων represents the same word and meaning; this is a disclosed orthographic feature, not evidence of OCR corruption.","proposed_reading":"συμπτώσεων","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","issue":"The plural subject of χερσεύσωσιν and γίνονται is not explicit. It may refer to the people who assemble and listen, to the discouragements, or to people understood through the image of land lying fallow. The translation retains the unresolved pronoun “they.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","issue":"The precise force of προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται remain uncertain. The sick may be brought to the multitude’s attention and then present themselves, or members of the previously unaware multitude may present themselves, perhaps by coming to the sick. “Visit them” would make that latter contextual inference explicit, but neither a visitation sense nor an object meaning “them” is separately expressed. The supplied reading is being translated provisionally, not emended.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"15","text":"The passengers, then, should remain steady, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiters should give reminders of the rewards. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, as a bow officer keeping watch, should respond to the words of the helmsman alone. The Messiah, as Savior-helmsman, should be loved, and he alone should be trusted regarding what he says. All should pray to God that they may sail with a fair wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction as they sail beside a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, naked, and distressed, and again at another time united, gathered together, and at rest, but also seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing their offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—by which I mean the sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive care).","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων","chosen":"The passengers, then, should remain steady, seated firmly in their own places","rationale":"Preserves both the call for steadiness and the image of passengers remaining firmly in their own assigned places."},{"source_quote":"σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν","chosen":"rocking or a list to one side","rationale":"Distinguishes general shaking or rocking from the vessel’s unequal inclination toward one side."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν","chosen":"The ship’s recruiters should give reminders of the rewards","rationale":"Retains the shipboard recruiting role and the reward sense of μισθούς without inserting a specific recipient absent from the clause."},{"source_quote":"καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς τὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","chosen":"should carefully prepare what each person needs","rationale":"Treats τὰ χρῄζοντα as the things needed by each person. The selected Greek’s τὰ reflects the recorded crop correction and is not a conjectural supplement in this draft."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","chosen":"should respond to the words of the helmsman alone","rationale":"The consulted evidence for ἀντιβάλλω includes conversational exchange of words, as in λόγους ἀ. πρὸς ἀλλήλους at Luke 24.17, supporting a responsive rendering. It does not directly attest the nautical relay of a command, so “respond” is preferred provisionally over “relay.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης","chosen":"The Messiah, as Savior-helmsman","rationale":"Renders independently titular χριστός as “Messiah” and preserves σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης as a combined designation without silently inserting a conjunction."},{"source_quote":"ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες","chosen":"seasick, dizzy, and vomiting","rationale":"Follows the escalating bodily imagery and the author’s immediate explanation of the final term as expelling disease-producing bile through confession."},{"source_quote":"προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν","chosen":"receive the saving health that comes from attentive care","rationale":"Preserves the medical image of accepting or receiving health that results from care or treatment."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ’ναῦται","issue":"The mark printed before ναῦται is not explained by ordinary elision, but this does not establish that it is accidental. Its editorial or typographic function remains unresolved; the translation treats it provisionally as nonlexical without altering the supplied transcription.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς τὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","issue":"The selected transcription reads τὰ. The recorded high-resolution crop review of a second copy of the same edition preserves the first letter’s horizontal head-bar and bent lower stroke, resolving an earlier transcription as -ὰ that resulted from a disconnected printing impression. This is a confirmed crop correction within the transcription record, not an unverified emendation of the supplied Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς","issue":"The mark printed before ἐγρηγορὼς is not required by the apparent syntax and is not explained by ordinary elision, but it may be an intentional editorial or typographic feature. The translation treats it provisionally as nonlexical without presenting an unmarked Greek form as an established correction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","issue":"The exact action expressed by ἀντιβαλλέτω remains uncertain. The attested conversational exchange sense supports “respond to the words,” while “echo” or “repeat the words” may fit the shipboard command context. “Relay the words” more specifically implies onward transmission and is not directly established by the consulted evidence. The comparison or collation sense of ἀντιβάλλω is also attested generally but is less readily intelligible here. No alteration of the supplied Greek is proposed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω","issue":"One ὡς governs the adjacent nouns σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης without καί. The main rendering “Savior-helmsman” preserves both as a combined designation. Possible interpretive alternatives include “as Savior, helmsman,” “as the saving helmsman,” and the explicitly coordinated “as Savior and helmsman,” but the last introduces a conjunction absent from the Greek. The exact grammatical relationship between the two designations remains uncertain.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐνούμενοι","issue":"The verified printed form ἐνούμενοι has smooth breathing. “United” understands it as the unity verb conventionally written ἑνόω, whose corresponding participle is ἑνούμενοι. The supplied Greek is retained; this is a disclosed orthographic identification, not an established OCR error or a silently normalized reading.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἀπερῶντες","issue":"The uncommon form is interpreted as vomiting or purging because the author immediately explains it through the expulsion of disease-producing bile and later uses ἀπεράσαντες in the same comparison. The general purgative sense is contextually strong, but the exact lexical formation remains uncertain.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
